summary: A 1934 35-ft Aermotor steel tower on West Fork Mountain in Idaho's Panhandle; the cabin is gone, the tower still stands, and climbing is not safe.

facts.design: 35-ft Aermotor steel X-brace tower with 7x7 cab; the 1934 frame residence cabin is gone
facts.status_note: Only the steel tower remains; the living cabin is gone and the lower stairs have been removed.

access.note: Reached on foot by Forest Service Trail #347. The tower itself is not safe for climbing.

visit.trail_note: About 3.4 miles on Trail #347 from the junction with Smith Creek-Red Top Trail #21; open mid-June through November, weather permitting.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Idaho Panhandle National Forests (Kaniksu National Forest cooperator)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Forest Fire Lookout give 1934; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934 or 1935. 1934 is used, with the other date noted in the story.

NHLR and the Forest Service trail page name the Idaho Panhandle National Forests; Idaho Fire Lookouts names the Kaniksu National Forest. NHLR lists Kaniksu as cooperator, so the Idaho Panhandle name is used.
NHLR, Forest Fire Lookout and Idaho Fire Lookouts all date abandonment to the 1950s without an exact year, so no abandonment event is entered.

notes_for_editor: Tower standing, cabin gone, lower stairs removed, climbing not safe (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Abandonment has no exact year; sources say the 1950s. Only two named lookouts: L.L. Hydron (1935, secondhand via Idaho Fire Lookouts' citation of the Bonners Ferry Herald) and Burt Callahan (1936). Forest name differs between NHLR/FS (Idaho Panhandle) and Idaho Fire Lookouts (Kaniksu). Record access 'unknown' is now public trail access; the tower is not to be climbed. Build year: 1934 vs 1934 or 1935.
